rationale: Python 3.14 semantics, static (cell never executed). runner is a nested function with ZERO parameters: it takes no factory argument, so bind_literal/parameter-miss paths (F1/F2 class) are never reached. CMD is assigned only at module level and is never bound in make_runner's or runner's local scope, so inside runner CMD is not a closure variable — CPython compiles it to LOAD_GLOBAL resolved against make_runner.__globals__ (the module dict) at every call. No closure cell exists to snapshot. Execution order: (1) CMD = ['pacman','-Q','r22-early'] binds the name; (2) make_runner() constructs runner, capturing NOTHING — runner.__closure__ is empty/None; (3) CMD = ['pacman','-S','r22-globallate'] rebinds the same module-global slot in-place; (4) runner() invokes the closure, LOAD_GLOBAL reads the CURRENT module binding: ['pacman','-S','r22-globallate']. subprocess.run receives the late list literally: exact argv ['pacman','-S','r22-globallate'], shlex.join => 'pacman -S r22-globallate', class host_mutation, evidence observed. Contrast the frozen-parameter class (F1): a factory ARGUMENT must bind at factory-call time, but a free module GLOBAL must resolve at invocation time — freezing it is the symmetric over-reach defect. A repaired ClosureFrame that snapshots the module literal env at factory creation would emit 'pacman -Q r22-early' (package_query); that row is the forbidden one. This variant therefore guards both directions: correct repair keeps parameters frozen at creation AND leaves unshadowed globals late-bound. expected_kind=exact: the full argv is statically determined with no unknown operand, so the sound result is exactly one observed row and zero unparsed; 'pacman -Q r22-early' must never appear as observed, and no fabricated row may be invented from the pre-rebind value.
